hook.line: Stop paying for expensive AI humanizers.
hook.visual: Very close, wide-angle face with hand to the lens, then a row of paid humanizer app icons that flash red as he dismisses them.

beats.what: Close-up command to stop paying; four paid humanizer app icons appear and tint red.
Screen splits: a white '100 day challenge' card with day dots above, him at his desk below, keyword captions in a white box.
The tool's app icon appears over him as he names it.
Top half shows a site listing humanizer alternatives as he lists its features.
Detector page with highlighted AI text as he names GPTZero and claims the tool bypasses it.
Paid competitor icons return in a row while he quotes their $20 monthly price.
The tool's logo large on white: free, no signup.
Feature pages: AI math solver, then the YouTube summarizer.
Web and iOS icons beside the logo show where to get it.
A fake comment bar reading 'Day 3' with a send button shows exactly what to comment.

why_it_works: The opening command names a cost the viewer already pays, so the 'free alternative' feels like money saved.
A numbered 100-day challenge card with progress dots signals a series, so viewers follow for the next day.
The comment CTA is drawn as a comment box already typed, so the action is copied, not imagined.
One keyword per caption in a white box over the split line keeps the eye between the screen and the face.
weaknesses: The video ends mid-sentence on 'and I'll', which feels clipped.
Product screens are mostly stills; nothing shows the tool working on real text.
Bypass-detection framing is risky and may not age well.
for_robert: Draw the CTA as a mock comment box with the exact keyword typed in; Fred could swim up and tap send at the end.
